sections.name: File setup

sections.name: template
sections.title: Fake model for tests
sections.what: Builds a grey box offset from its own centre on purpose, so the test checks that fitting moves it to the centre.
sections.why: An off-centre box shows whether the centring logic works.
sections.watch_out: The fake box is not a real GLB file, so real file quirks are not covered.

sections.name: size
sections.title: Measure an object's size
sections.what: Returns the width, height and depth of an object's outer box, after updating its position data.

sections.watch_out: The position update must run first, otherwise the size can be stale.

sections.name: detailed model library
sections.title: Checks for fitting, repeating and unknown names
sections.what: Four checks: a model fits its box, is centred, and gets its own material key; a long row repeats six times along its length; a tower stacks six floors to its full height; an unknown name returns nothing.
sections.why: Each one covers a behaviour the app relies on for detailed element models.
sections.watch_out: Tests register into a shared store, so they depend on each other's names and on run order.

summary: Tests that detailed 3D element models are sized, centred, repeated and given their own materials correctly.
purpose: Check the fitting logic in modelLibrary.ts using simple box stand-ins instead of real model files.
why: Likely reason: fitting is easy to get subtly wrong, for example in size, centring or shared materials, so the tests protect those behaviours.
how: Creates a fake box template that is deliberately off-centre, registers it under a name, then builds instances for a tank, a row repeated along one axis, a tower stacking floors, and an unknown name. It checks the resulting size, centring, number of copies, and material key.
inputs: Fake template boxes created inside the test and fixed dimension values.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: Tests use fake geometry, not the real GLB model files, so they do not prove the real files load or look right. Registered names are stored in a shared store, so test order can matter.
debug: If a test fails, compare the registered native size with the requested size and the repeat settings. The failing assertion names the value that did not match.
